headline: Recommended placing on file petitions on roaming cats and miniature liquor bottle sales; also filed winter shelter and opioid fund items.
summary: Councilors reviewed a petition on roaming cats and a petition to ban miniature alcohol bottles. Both were recommended for filing. Other items covered winter overflow shelters, opioid settlement funds, the Metrik data platform, Sticker Shock Campaign, and the Worcester Senior Center, and all were recommended for filing too.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 24, 2026 meeting.
Recommended placing the petition on rules for roaming cats on file.
Recommended placing the petition to ban miniature alcohol bottles on file.
Recommended placing the Metrik public health data platform review on file.
Recommended placing the Sticker Shock Campaign meeting request on file.
Recommended placing the request for public hearings on winter emergency shelters on file.
Recommended placing the opioid settlement allocation communication on file.
Recommended placing the Worcester Senior Center communication on file.

Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the impersonation 
of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting payments be 
made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions. All official 
emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an @worcesterma.gov email 
address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail on the City of 
Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always include your 
specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, and location . 
The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.

. Approval of the Minutes 2 
Order - That the City Council Standing Committee of Public Health and Human Services 
hereby approves the minutes of the Public Health and Human Services Committee 
meeting on August 24, 2026.
a.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and moved to adopt the item. Order adopted
. Miscellaneous Items 3 
October 19, 2026 Page 2 of 10Public Health and Human Services Committee
Petition of Cristina DePina request regulations be established to ensure cats are not 
allowed to roam freely.
# 10d CC September 8, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Cristina DePina, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
2. Arlene Rosario, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed an estimated number of owned cats and the estimated 
number of thirty thousand (30,000) feral and /or stray cats in the city that roam freely with 
Speaker #1. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor Toomey, who discussed the feasibility of the 
Animal Control Unit enforcing additional animal related regulations. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen then brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Manager provide City Council with a report detailing best methods practiced by other cities and 
towns to mitigate owned cats from roaming freely throughout the city. Further, request said 
report include an estimated cost analysis to implement and enforce such potential regulation 
changes and any incentives for pet owners to spay/neuter their cats.”
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed the estimated one hundred (100) trap-neuter-release 
(TNR) cats trapped in six (6) months within a half mile radius in District 4, the process relative to 
TNR, the importance of educating the public of responsible pet ownership, and an estimated 
amount of trappers in the city dedicated to TNR with Speaker #2.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor Toomey, who spoke concerning the feasibility 
of the Department of Health and Human Services working with the Veterinary Assisting Program 
at Worcester Technical High School to brainstorm best practices relative to educating the public of 
responsible pet ownership.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed the feasibility relative to the Department of Health and 
Human Services to commit to assisting with the free roaming cat issue in the city with the 
Commissioner of Health and Human Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen then discussed issues related to cats being left behind by owners due 
to financial hardships, such as homelessness, and/or due to unforeseen animal free living 
arrangements with Speaker #2.   
Chairperson Councilor Rosen then moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File

Petition of Brian Dutremble request the banning of the sale of miniature alcohol bottles , 
or "nips," in the city to reduce litter and alcohol abuse.
# 8c CC August 18, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and discussed a history of the City Council’s 
discussions relative to reducing miniature alcohol bottle litter throughout the city. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized the following Speaker:
1. Jim Vasiliadis, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to the item
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed negative financial impacts banning miniature alcohol 
bottles would have on small liquor sale businesses and the demographic of customers who 
typically purchase miniature alcohol bottles with Speaker #1.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor Toomey, who discussed feasible local 
incentives for small liquor sale businesses to implement for the purpose of accepting returned 
miniature alcohol bottles with Speaker #1. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor King, who spoke concerning the item with the 
Deputy City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File

Order of Councilor Gary Rosen and Councilor Khrystian E. King - Request Standing 
Committee on Public Health and Human Services review Metrik, the Commonwealth 's 
new public health data and workflow platform. With Metrik, the Department of Public 
Health (DPH) strives to help municipalities reduce administrative burdens, improve 
visibility into local trends, enhance the ability of communities to provide efficient and 
effective public health services, and ensure access to the same secure, high-quality 
reporting tools throughout the Commonwealth.
# 17m CC April 28, 2026
c.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Inspectional 
Services, who provided an overview relative to the state’s public health data and workflow 
platform, Metrik, which included the city working with Metrik and state personnel to help 
develop the program, the process relative to integrate Metrik with the city’s current program , 
OpenGov, the ability to analyze trends within different communities across the state, highlighted 
the notion Metrik currently remains in development, and the process relative for data recorded in 
OpenGov be transmitted to Metrik. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor Toomey, who discussed the feasibility relative 
for Metrik to be utilized interdepartmentally to encompass all city departments and highlighted 
the Department of Health and Human Services, the Division of Public Health, and the Department 
of Inspectional Services as the only city entities to utilize Metrik with the Commissioner of 
Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor King, who discussed potential costs associated 
with the city utilizing Metrik and highlighted the importance relative to streamlining received 
complaints, inspections, and other reports with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen then discussed the importance relative to informing City Council of 
updates and /or changes as the program remains in development with the Commissioner of 
Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor King, who discussed the Department of 
Inspectional Services’ staffing capacity, the eight (8) unfilled positions assigned to the department , 
and challenges relative to onboarding new employees to fill said unfilled positions with the 
Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File
October 19, 2026 Page 5 of 10Public Health and Human Services Committee
Order of Councilor Gary Rosen - Request Standing Committee on Public Health and 
Human Services meet with representatives of the Department of Public Health, the 
Division of Youth Opportunities, the Worcester Police Department and the seven (7) city 
teens who worked on the city’s Sticker Shock Campaign, for the purpose of discussing 
the successes of the program and further supporting similar initiatives in the future. Said 
Sticker Shock Campaign is designed to discourage adults from purchasing alcohol for 
minors, reinforce ID checks at the point of sale, is a youth -led public health effort aimed 
at curbing underage drinking before it starts, and is part of a broader set of prevention 
initiatives combining education, enforcement and community outreach.
# 10q CC March 31, 2026
d.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and recognized Councilor Toomey, who moved to 
recuse herself from the item and left the room. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized the WPD Alcohol Unit Sgt ., who provided an overview 
relative to the Worcester Police Department’s (WPD) collaborative work with the Alcoholic 
Beverage Control Commission (ABCC) to address underage drinking, the process relative to 
facilitate underage alcohol sales sting operations, and trends observed relative to underage alcohol 
sale violations. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed the Sticker Shock Campaign primarily being within the 
purview of the Division of Public Health with the Director of Youth Opportunities.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized the Director of Public Health, who provided an overview 
relative the city’s Sticker Shock Campaign, an evidence -based public health strategy to raise 
awareness around underage drinking and to prevent adults from purchasing alcohol for minors , 
which also included Worcester Public School (WPS) data analyzed relative to a youth health 
survey as relates to alcohol purchases and consumption, and efforts made by the Worcester youth 
who participated in the campaign. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor King, who discussed the prevalence of adults 
purchasing alcohol for minors, efforts made to work with local colleges and universities to educate 
incoming students about underage drinking risks during their first -year orientations, and 
approximately seven percent (7%) of WPS students who report to drink alcohol also report 
providing money to individuals to purchase alcohol on their behalf with the WPD Alcohol Unit 
Sgt. And Director of Public Health. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File
October 19, 2026 Page 6 of 10Public Health and Human Services Committee
Order of Councilor Gary Rosen, Councilor Morris A. Bergman, Councilor Robert A . 
Bilotta, Councilor Tony Economou, Councilor John P. Fresolo, Councilor Khrystian E . 
King, Councilor Satya B. Mitra, Councilor Luis A. Ojeda, Councilor Jose A. Rivera, 
Councilor Kathleen M. Toomey and Mayor Joseph M. Petty - Request Standing 
Committee on Public Health and Human Services hold one or more public hearings, far 
in advance of next winter, in an effort to help the city identify and to secure a sufficient 
number of safe and secure emergency shelter locations that serve the needs of the 
unhoused population during the winter of 2026-2027. Further, request said public 
hearings should also focus on strategies to increase the number of individuals who 
volunteer at said emergency shelter locations as well as training for said individuals.
# 9i CC February 3, 2026
e.
In Committee April 6, 2026 - Held
October 19, 2026 Page 7 of 10Public Health and Human Services Committee
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Health and 
Human Services, who discussed the process relative for the city to apply for available winter 
shelter funding with anticipation of being granted state funding in early November, plans to 
provide a minimum of sixty (60) individual overflow beds for winter shelter services, conversations 
with state administration to stress the critical need for overflow winter shelter operations in the 
city, alternate plans to continue with the sixty (60) bed minimum in the event state funding is not 
granted, and the expectation to open winter overflow shelters on December 1, 2026. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed the state funded overflow winter shelter request for 
proposal (RFP) amount of $1.5 million with the requirement for the Department of Health and 
Human Services to partner with experienced community organizations, overflow winter shelter 
location negotiations, the winter overflow shelter sites providing both overnight and daytime 
services, and a timeline associated with opening the day shelter in April 2027 with the 
Commissioner of Health and Human Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor Toomey, who discussed the process relative 
for the overflow winter shelter services ensure individuals have access to food, such as close 
proximity and /or transportation to food pantries with the Commissioner of Health and Human 
Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor King, who spoke concerning the status of 
overflow winter shelter location identification, the Department of Health and Human Services 
identifying the need for sixty (60) to sixty -five (65) individual beds, the city’s historical capacity of 
thirty-six (36) available individual beds for overflow winter shelter, the number of reported 
chronically unsheltered individuals in the city compared to available overflow individual overflow 
beds, and strategies implemented to ensure adequate shelter staff capacity with the Commissioner 
of Health and Human Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed the intention for the committee to continue discussing 
topics related to unsheltered individuals and shelter services with Councilor King and the 
Commissioner of Health and Human Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed supplemental location options in the event state funding 
be granted but no locations are agreed upon with the Commissioner of Health and Human 
Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen then moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File
. Communications of the City Manager 4 
October 19, 2026 Page 8 of 10Public Health and Human Services Committee
Transmitting Informational Communication Relative to the City of Worcester Opioid 
Allocation.
# 8.19B CM September 15, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and recognized Councilor Toomey, who moved to 
recuse herself from the item and left the room. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Health and Human 
Services, who provided an overview relative to the city’s prior, pending, and future use and 
allocations of opioid settlement funds, best practices relative to refining the process relative to 
identifying priority areas, the process relative to reviewing request for proposal (RFP) 
applications, and an estimated amount of funds received annually based on available settlements. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed the importance relative to remaining transparent 
throughout the RFP application processes, the process relative to assessing programs’ use of 
awarded funds, decreased overdose related deaths in the city, and the distribution of Narcan 
throughout the city with the Assistant Commissioner of Health and Human Services.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor King, who spoke concerning the Assistant 
Commissioner of Health and Human Services’ title and involvement at the time of the first round 
of distributing settlement funds, the process relative to replace Community Healthlink’s crisis 
response model, shower access and supportive services, the process relative to measuring the 
efficacy related to the work completed by awardees under contract, funding allocations with 
awarded grants from prior fiscal years, funding allocated to the women’s shelter, the process 
relative to maximize community feedback and coordination, the process relative to allocating 
funds as relates to culturally responsive strategies, clarified opioid settlement funds are used for 
general substance abuse and /or misuse in addition to opioid specific related matters, and available 
funding to combat the rising xylazine epidemic with the Assistant Commissioner of Health and 
Human Services.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Manager request Commissioner of Health and Human Services provide City Council with a 
report detailing xylazine related overdoses in the city.”
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed the operation status of Community Healthlink and the 
member demographic relative to the stakeholder review committee for opioid settlement funds 
with the Assistant Commissioner of Health and Human Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File
Chairman's Orders
Request City Manager request Commissioner of Health and Human Services provide 
City Council with a report detailing xylazine related overdoses in the city.
October 19, 2026 Page 9 of 10Public Health and Human Services Committee
Transmitting informational communication relative to the Worcester Senior Center.
# 22.19A CM June 2, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen read the item and recognized the Director of Elder Affairs, who 
provided an overview relative to the Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) Worcester Senior Center Participant 
Survey Report. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen discussed an estimated three hundred (300) to five hundred (500) 
daily patrons who utilize the Senior Center, an estimated thirteen hundred (1,300) registered 
fitness center members, and outreach methods used to inform residents of available resources for 
the city’s senior residents with the Director of Elder Affairs. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor King, who highlighted the diverse programs 
offered at the Worcester Senior Center.
Chairperson Councilor Rosen recognized Councilor Toomey, who discussed the positive impact 
the Worcester Senior Center has for patron’s mental health. 
Chairperson Councilor Rosen moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File
